name: Hatah (Esther's servant)
title: Queen Esther's trusted courtier
summary: Hatah was a courtier appointed by King Ahasuerus to serve Queen Esther. He acted as a messenger between Esther and her cousin Mordecai during a critical period when the fate of the Jewish people hung in the balance. His faithful service enabled the communication that led to the deliverance of the Jewish nation.

keyEvents.title: Appointed as Esther's servant
keyEvents.description: Hatah was one of the courtiers whom the king had assigned to serve Queen Esther in her chambers within the palace.

keyEvents.title: Messenger between Esther and Mordecai
keyEvents.description: When Mordecai mourned in sackcloth and ashes at the king's gate, Esther sent Hatah out to find out what was wrong and why Mordecai was acting this way.

keyEvents.title: Bearer of Haman's evil plan
keyEvents.description: Hatah received information from Mordecai about Haman's plan to destroy the Jews, including a copy of the decree, and brought it back to Esther.

keyEvents.title: Conveyer of Esther's reply
keyEvents.description: Hatah conveyed Esther's explanation to Mordecai about her father by going uninvited to the king, and then brought Mordecai's challenge back to her.
